To: [Health plan name and appeals department]

Re: Appeal of denial of cervical fusion  
Member: Riley Grant  
Member ID: W510384895  
Reference number: POC-E288D08833-89297  
Requested service: Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion  
CPT: 22551  
Date of denial notice: August 4, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal the denial of the requested C5-C6 anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, CPT 22551. This appeal addresses the stated medical-necessity basis for the denial.

The submitted clinical records establish a persistent, progressive cervical condition with objective neurologic involvement:

- Riley has had 12 months of progressive neck pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- Riley completed 16 supervised physical-therapy visits over eight weeks, from May 17, 2026, through July 12, 2026. Treatment included cervical traction and postural training, and the physical-therapy discharge note documents the completed course.
- Riley used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 26, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- A cervical MRI performed June 24, 2026, showed a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and compression of the C6 nerve root.
- Riley has radicular pain and numbness extending into the right thumb and index finger, together with weakness.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged cervical level.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use. Riley is a nonsmoker, has a BMI of 29, and has no documented factor in the submitted records that would independently preclude surgery.
- Lindqvist, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, recommended the requested procedure.

These records demonstrate persistent symptoms despite substantial nonsurgical treatment, objective imaging showing severe foraminal narrowing and nerve-root compression, and clinical findings that correspond to the affected level and nerve distribution. The symptoms are functionally significant and include weakness and neurologic sensory changes, not pain alone. The limited and temporary response to injection further supports that conservative treatment has not adequately resolved the condition.

I request that the denial be reversed and that authorization for the requested C5-C6 procedure be approved.

The publicly available materials reviewed for this appeal did not establish which insurer or managed-care plan issued this determination. They also did not provide the specific clinical-review criteria applied to Riley. Please provide, with the appeal decision:

1. The exact medical-necessity criteria applied to CPT 22551;
2. The specific criterion or criteria determined not to be satisfied;
3. The clinical rationale for that determination;
4. The records and clinical information reviewed; and
5. A copy of any clinical-review guideline or other policy used in deciding this request.

The governing criteria were not available in the denial materials provided to Riley, so this appeal explains medical necessity from the clinical record rather than quoting plan criteria.

Please conduct a complete clinical reconsideration by a physician qualified in spine surgery or orthopedic surgery. If additional information is required, please contact Lindqvist, MD, or notify me promptly so the requested information can be supplied.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and send the appeal decision in writing.

Sincerely,

Riley Grant  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Enclosures: Denial notice; MRI report dated June 24, 2026; physical-therapy discharge note; medication and injection records; orthopedic evaluation; supporting clinical records
